post.summary: Simulate an AoE4 build order and report its timings.
post.description: Simulates one AoE4 build order for one horizon and returns the timings. The simulation is deterministic: the same request and game data always give the same body. Validation runs in two stages; at most 100 issues are listed and the rest are counted in omittedIssues. A body that is not a JSON object (an array, string, number or null) gives one syntax issue and nothing else is checked. Otherwise the order stage runs (a body with a text key is rejected with one syntax issue and buildOrder is not checked; else buildOrder is required and validated) and then the inputs stage always runs too, even when the order stage failed; issues list order-stage issues first, then inputs issues, and error is the first issue message. Issue location: no issue carries line; an issue on a step carries step; an issue on start, on inputs, or on the request shape carries neither. Absent inputs fields at any depth take their defaults. Two framework responses have no schema and happen before the handler runs: a body that is not valid JSON is a 400 with the plain-text body Invalid JSON, and a body over the 1 MB default body limit is a 413 with a plain-text body.

FightRequest.description: The two armies and the number of battles to run. Cross-field rules, checked by the server rather than this schema: for each side, regulars + elites must be at most 10 (leaders are not counted), and regulars + elites = 0 is invalid. Validation order, where the first failure is the one reported: the method must be POST; the body must be a JSON object; the six army fields in the order attack-regs, attack-elts, attack-ldrs, defend-regs, defend-elts, defend-ldrs; the per-side rules, attack then defend; then battles. The server ignores unknown extra keys; this schema is deliberately stricter and rejects them.

attack-regs.description: Regular units in the attacking army. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 10.

attack-elts.description: Elite units in the attacking army. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 10.

attack-ldrs.description: Leaders in the attacking army. Leaders do not count toward the army's unit limit. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 5.

defend-regs.description: Regular units in the defending army. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 10.

defend-elts.description: Elite units in the defending army. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 10.

defend-ldrs.description: Leaders in the defending army. Leaders do not count toward the army's unit limit. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 0 and 5.

battles.description: Number of independent battles to simulate. Sent as a JSON integer or as a string of decimal digits (leading zeros allowed); either form must be between 1 and 100000.

FightResponse.description: Statistics over all simulated battles. The submitted armies are not echoed back.

rounds.description: How many rounds the battles lasted.

survivors.description: What the winning side had left.

hitsPerRound.description: How many hits each side scored per round.

FightError.description: Error body for a rejected request.

error.description: Human-readable reason the request was rejected. A field error names the field.

FightOutcomes.description: One entry per outcome kind; counts over all kinds sum to battles, and a kind that never occurred has count 0. Later versions may add outcome kinds with the same {count, frequency} shape; clients must tolerate unknown keys.

attacker.description: Only the attacker has regulars or elites left.

defender.description: Only the defender has regulars or elites left.

tie.description: Both armies were eliminated in the same round.

count.description: Battles that ended with this outcome.

RoundStats.description: Rounds per battle over all battles, every outcome included. median, p10 and p90 use the nearest-rank method: sort the round counts ascending and take the value at 1-based rank ceil(p * battles / 100).

median.description: 50th percentile, nearest rank (the lower middle value for an even number of battles).

FightSurvivors.description: For each side, the distribution of its surviving (regulars, elites) at the end of the battles it won. Leaders are not part of a combination, and ties contribute nothing. Elements are sorted by count, then regulars, then elites, all descending.

attacker.description: Surviving units of the attacker over the battles it won, one element per combination that occurred; empty when the attacker never won.

defender.description: Surviving units of the defender over the battles it won, one element per combination that occurred; empty when the defender never won.

SurvivorCombination.description: One combination of surviving regulars and elites on the winning side.

count.description: Wins by this side that ended with this combination.

HitsPerRound.description: Hit-count distribution per side, pooled across all rounds of all battles (combat and leader hits together). The denominator is the total rounds.

attacker.description: Index k is the share of all rounds in which the attacker scored exactly k hits.

defender.description: Index k is the share of all rounds in which the defender scored exactly k hits.

SimulateRequest.description: One simulation request: buildOrder (JSON, required) plus optional inputs. The paste-format text field was removed in 2.0.0: a body with a text key (any value, null included) is rejected with the syntax issue "request: text is no longer accepted; convert the paste to buildOrder and send that", even when buildOrder is also sent. Convert the paste format with the page or with textToBuildOrder and send the result as buildOrder. Unknown extra keys other than text are ignored.

buildOrder.description: The build order as JSON, at most 200 steps. Issues on a step carry step and never line; issues on start carry neither.

inputs.description: Simulation inputs; every absent field, at any depth, takes its default. Issues here carry neither step nor line.

BuildOrder.description: A build order: steps run in list order, each once its trigger holds and every earlier non-reaction step has started; a reaction starts once its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps. Unknown extra keys are ignored.

civ.description: Civilization; only english is supported. Any other string is an unknown-id issue.

name.description: Display name of the build order.

source.description: Where the build order comes from, for example a guide URL.

start.description: The t=0 villager split and rally; omitted keeps the civ split and sets no rally.

steps.description: The steps, at most 200. More is one out-of-range issue and no step is checked.

BuildStart.description: Starting state overrides. Both fields are optional; {} is valid. Unknown extra keys are ignored.

villagers.description: Villagers per node ref at t=0, each 0..200. When present it replaces the civ split whole (omitted nodes get 0) and the values must sum to the civ starting count (6 for english), else an invalid issue. Node keys are checked like any node ref (for example unknown-id for iron, invalid for gold#1).

rally.description: Rally node at t=0 for the starting villager producers. Required (as an invalid issue) when a starting building produces villagers, which is true for english (capital-town-center).

BuildStep.description: One step, a oneOf on the action const. Ids are aoe4world baseIds. A step that is not an object, has an unknown action, or a missing or mistyped field is a syntax issue. Unknown extra keys are ignored.

oneOf.description: Queue units at a producer. Without count production is continuous until a later produce or pause on that producer.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

producer.description: baseId of the producing building; must be a producedBy building of the unit (else invalid).

instance.description: 1-based instance of the producer to target, 1..200; omitted targets every instance of that baseId.

unit.description: baseId of the unit to produce.

count.description: Units to produce, 1..200; omitted means continuous.

rally.description: Villager only (else invalid): sets the producer rally for villagers it spawns from this step on.

walkSeconds.description: Walk in seconds for the rally walk; only allowed with rally (else invalid), 0..60 (decimals allowed); omitted inherits inputs.walkSeconds.

oneOf.description: Set the rally node of a villager producer for villagers spawned from this step on; costs nothing and completes when it starts.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

producer.description: baseId of a villager producer (else invalid).

instance.description: 1-based instance of the producer to target, 1..200; omitted targets every instance of that baseId.

walkSeconds.description: Walk in seconds for the rally walk of every villager it routes, 0..60 (decimals allowed); omitted inherits inputs.walkSeconds.

oneOf.description: Stop production at a producer; completes when it starts.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

instance.description: 1-based instance of the producer to target, 1..200; omitted targets every instance of that baseId.

oneOf.description: Pull villagers off a node to construct a building, then send them to a node.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

building.description: baseId of the building to construct.

from.description: Node ref the builders are taken from, gathering first and then idle; the step waits until it holds builders villagers.

then.description: Node ref the builders go to afterwards; default from. When it is the node the building creates (farm for a farm), they start there at completion with no walk back.

walkSeconds.description: Walk in seconds for each build leg, 0..60 (decimals allowed); omitted inherits inputs.walkSeconds.

oneOf.description: Research a technology or veterancy upgrade. A technology an earlier research step already names is invalid.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

tech.description: baseId of the technology; one whose effects cannot be simulated is unsupported-tech or unknown-tech-effect.

at.description: baseId of the building to research it at; must be a producedBy building of the technology (else invalid). Omitted uses the technology producedBy.

oneOf.description: Move villagers between gather nodes.

trigger.description: When the step may start; omitted means no condition.

reaction.description: Marks the step as a reaction: it arms as soon as its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps, and never delays later steps. Only a step with a depleted trigger can be a reaction; a schema cannot express that rule, so the server is authoritative and rejects any other reaction with an invalid issue.

oneOf.description: Villagers to move, 1..200; the step waits until from holds that many, gathering or idle.
Every villager at from when the step starts, gathering or idle; never waits, and with none there it completes at once moving nobody.

count.description: Villagers to move: a count or all.

from.description: Node ref the villagers leave, gathering first and then idle.

to.description: Node ref the villagers go to; arriving at a depleted ref leaves them idle.

walkSeconds.description: Walk in seconds for the move, 0..60 (decimals allowed); omitted inherits inputs.walkSeconds.

Trigger.description: A oneOf on the kind const. A trigger whose kind is not time, villagers, depleted or bank is invalid under this schema, and the server rejects it with an unknown-trigger-kind issue; a trigger that is not an object or has a mistyped field is a syntax issue.

oneOf.description: Holds from a game time on.
Holds once the villager count reaches count.
Holds from the instant a node ref runs out on; never for a ref that does not run out by durationSeconds (an infinite amount, no gatherers, or stock left).

node.description: Node ref to watch; a gold deposit named only here still gets its own stock and depletions entry.

oneOf.description: Holds once the bank of resource reaches atLeast; armed at the exact instant income reaches it.

GatherNodeId.description: A gather node villagers work at.

FiniteGatherNodeId.description: A gather node that can run out; farm and wood never do.

DepositRef.description: A numbered gold deposit, gold#2 to gold#8. Deposit 1 is written plain gold.

NodeRef.description: A gather node or a numbered gold deposit.

oneOf.description: A gather node; gold is gold deposit 1.
A numbered gold deposit.

FiniteNodeRef.description: A node ref that can run out: a finite gather node or a numbered gold deposit.

oneOf.description: A finite gather node; gold is gold deposit 1.
A numbered gold deposit.

SimInputOverrides.description: Simulation input overrides. Every property is optional and every absent field takes its default at any depth: trips merges per node and then per field, influenceCoverage and nodeAmounts per key. An out-of-range value is an out-of-range issue whose message names its path, for example inputs.trips.farm.walkSecondsCamp. Unknown extra keys are ignored.

trips.description: Per-node gather trip overrides; nodes and fields left out keep the rules/base.json defaults. An unknown node key is an unknown-id issue.

walkSeconds.description: Base walk in seconds per task switch (move, build legs, rally, auto-house), 0..60; default from rules/base.json.

autoHouses.description: Whether houses are built automatically to stay ahead of supply.

houseBuilders.description: Villagers that build each automatic house, 1..200.

houseBuilderSource.description: Preferred node automatic house builders are taken from.

influenceCoverage.description: Share of gatherers inside a building influence once one exists, keyed by building baseId, each 0..1; keys left out keep their default ({ mill: 1 }). An unknown building key is an unknown-id issue.

nodeAmounts.description: Starting stock per finite node ref, each an integer 0..100000 or null for infinite; keys left out keep their default, gatherNodes.<node>.amount in rules/base.json (gold#k uses gold's), which ships for all six finite nodes; null makes a node infinite. gold sets deposit 1 only. farm and wood never run out and are invalid keys. An override for a deposit the order does not name is accepted and unused.

TripInputOverrides.description: Gather trip overrides for one node. Every property is optional; absent ones keep the node default. Unknown extra keys are ignored.

walkSecondsCamp.description: Walk in seconds between the node and a drop-off camp, 0..60.

walkSecondsTownCenter.description: Walk in seconds between the node and a town center, 0..60.

dropOffSeconds.description: Seconds spent dropping off a load, 0..30.

SimulationResult.description: The simulated timings. Every series has one value per entry of times.

times.description: Sample times in seconds: 0, s, 2s, ... for s = sampleSeconds, up to and including durationSeconds; when durationSeconds is not a multiple of s the last sample is durationSeconds.

unitsProduced.description: One series per unit entry and tier that held a produced unit at some instant, ordered by that first instant, then unitId; starting units never appear.

gatherRates.description: Income per minute for each resource at each sample.

food.description: Income per minute of this resource at each sample.

wood.description: Income per minute of this resource at each sample.

gold.description: Income per minute of this resource at each sample.

stone.description: Income per minute of this resource at each sample.

floating.description: Banked, unspent amount of each resource at each sample.

food.description: Banked amount of this resource at each sample.

wood.description: Banked amount of this resource at each sample.

gold.description: Banked amount of this resource at each sample.

stone.description: Banked amount of this resource at each sample.

gathered.description: Cumulative amount of each resource gathered up to each sample; starting resources are excluded.

food.description: Cumulative amount of this resource gathered up to each sample.

wood.description: Cumulative amount of this resource gathered up to each sample.

gold.description: Cumulative amount of this resource gathered up to each sample.

stone.description: Cumulative amount of this resource gathered up to each sample.

spent.description: Cumulative resources paid by category (food, wood, gold and stone summed) at each sample; a payment at a sample time is included.

spawnedPopulation.description: Popcap of spawned villagers and units at each sample, start population included; paid units still in production are not counted.

populationCapReachedAt.description: Instant spawnedPopulation first reached the population cap (a spawn instant, not a sample time), or null.

steps.description: One timing per build order step, in step order.

reachedAt.description: Game time in seconds the age was reached.

ages.description: Each age reached and when, starting age first.

notes.description: Non-fatal notes about technologies whose effects are not all simulated.

depletions.description: One entry per finite node ref the run uses (the six finite nodes plus every gold deposit the order names), in node-ref order. The six finite nodes are always present; amount is null when infinite, depletedAt null while stocked.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings sorted by at; at equal at, node warnings come first in node-ref order with node-depleted before idle-arrival for one ref, then farm-idle, then step-stuck by step, then auto-houses-never-start and auto-houses-held, never-start first. Holds node-depleted and idle-arrival warnings when a finite node runs out (see nodeAmounts), at most one farm-idle warning when villagers wait idle at farm with every built farm taken, a step-stuck warning for each step still waiting at durationSeconds, and, with autoHouses on, at most one auto-houses-never-start (the last build house step is a reaction that never fired) and at most one auto-houses-held (production sat at the supply limit while that step had not started).

markers.description: One marker per age reached after the start age and per completed research, sorted by at, then kind, then label.

UnitSeries.description: Produced units at one unit entry and tier over time. A veterancy upgrade moves units to a higher tier's series; the series of one baseId sum to its cumulative produced units.

counts.description: Produced units at this entry's tier at each sample time; a series whose units all moved to a higher tier stays at 0.

StepTiming.description: Timing of one step at the horizon.

status.description: State of the step at durationSeconds.

armedAt.description: When the trigger held and every earlier non-reaction step had started; a reaction arms when its trigger holds, without waiting for earlier steps. null if never.

startedAt.description: When the step started (paid and supply allowed); null if never.

completedAt.description: When the step finished; null if not by durationSeconds.

waitSeconds.description: startedAt - armedAt once the step has started; 0 before it starts.

waitingOn.description: Why the step has not started: the reason of its last failed check while waiting, trigger or earlier-step when not-reached, null once started.

waitBreakdown.description: Seconds from armedAt spent on each reason; a reason with 0 seconds is absent. Sums to waitSeconds once started, and to the time from armedAt to durationSeconds while waiting.

BuildOrderIssue.description: One problem with the request; any issue means nothing was simulated.

code.description: syntax: shape or spelling; unknown-trigger-kind: trigger kind other than time, villagers, depleted or bank; unknown-id: id not in the civ data; unsupported-tech and unknown-tech-effect: a technology that cannot be simulated; out-of-range: a number outside its bound, non-integer where an integer is required, or non-finite; invalid: a cross-field rule fails.

message.description: Human-readable reason, naming the step and the offending id, kind or property.

step.description: 0-based index of the step the issue is on; absent for start, inputs and request-level issues.

line.description: 1-based line of a paste; this API never sets it. It is set only on issues from the page-side conversion of the paste format to buildOrder.

suggestion.description: The nearest valid id; present only on unknown-id and unknown-trigger-kind issues.

BuildOrderNote.description: A non-fatal note on a research step.

code.description: tech-effect-ignored: some effect properties are ignored (listed); tech-effect-unmodeled: the technology has no simulated effect.

severity.description: Severity of this note; every note is info.

message.description: Human-readable note that names the technology by id (baseId).

properties.description: Effect properties not simulated; empty for tech-effect-unmodeled.

Severity.description: How serious a message is, most severe first. No result item is error today; request errors are the 400 issues.

StepWait.description: Why a step has not started yet.

NodeDepletion.description: Starting stock and run-out time of one node ref the run uses.

amount.description: Starting stock; null when the ref is infinite.

depletedAt.description: Game time in seconds the ref ran out; null if it still had stock at durationSeconds.

SimWarning.description: A non-fatal warning about the run, a oneOf tagged by the code const.

oneOf.description: A node ref ran out. severity is warning when villagers were left idle there, else info.

message.description: Human-readable warning naming the node by id.

node.description: The node ref the warning is about.

at.description: Game time in seconds the ref ran out.

idleVillagers.description: Villagers idle at the ref at the end of the run-out instant.

oneOf.description: Villagers arrived at a node ref that had already run out and are idle; severity is warning.

message.description: Human-readable warning naming the node by id.

node.description: The node ref the warning is about.

at.description: Game time in seconds of the first such arrival.

idleVillagers.description: Total villagers that arrived idle there by durationSeconds.

oneOf.description: Villagers arrived, or started, at farm with one villager per built farm already gathering, and wait idle until a farm is built; at most one per run; severity is warning.

message.description: Human-readable warning with the villager count and the first time.

at.description: Game time in seconds of the first villager left idle for lack of a farm.

idleVillagers.description: Total villagers that arrived, or started, at farm with no free farm by durationSeconds, including those a farm took later.

oneOf.description: A step was still waiting at durationSeconds; severity is warning.

message.description: Human-readable warning naming the step (1-based) and its action.

waitingOn.description: What the step was waiting on at durationSeconds.

at.description: Game time in seconds the step was armed.

oneOf.description: With autoHouses on, the order's last build house step is a reaction that never fired by durationSeconds, so no auto-house is built; severity is warning.

severity.description: Severity of this warning; always warning.

message.description: Human-readable warning naming the step (1-based) and durationSeconds as m:ss.

step.description: 0-based index of the order's last build house step, the step auto-houses wait for.

at.description: Always 0: the condition holds for the whole run.

oneOf.description: With autoHouses on and supply below the max population cap, production was held at the supply limit while the order's last build house step had not started, which keeps auto-houses off; severity is warning.

severity.description: Severity of this warning; always warning.

message.description: Human-readable warning naming the held seconds and the first held instant as m:ss, and the step (1-based).

step.description: 0-based index of the order's last build house step, the step auto-houses wait for.

at.description: Game time in seconds of the first instant production was held.

seconds.description: Total seconds production was held: the sum of every interval from a held instant to the next simulation instant.

SimulateError.description: Error body for a rejected request; nothing was simulated.

error.description: The message of the first issue.

issues.description: The first 100 issues found: order-stage issues first (buildOrder), then inputs issues.

omittedIssues.description: Count of issues dropped past the 100-issue cap; absent when none were dropped.

SpendCategory.description: What a payment bought: villager production, any other unit, a building (including auto-houses) or a technology.

ChartMarkerKind.description: What a chart marker marks: an age-up, or a completed research classified as economy, unit-tier, blacksmith or other.

ChartMarker.description: A point on the time axis where an age was reached or a research completed.

label.description: Age name (Feudal, Castle, Imperial) for age-up, else the researched tech's baseId.

at.description: Game time in seconds the age was reached or the research completed.
